songbird.label: The clockwork songbird
songbird.moment: Wind her up and she sings. A real tūī taught her the song.
songbird.moment_quiet: Wind her up. Turn the sound on, by the bell, and you'll hear her sing.

scales.label: The scales
scales.moment: Three spoons of chia to a cup of milk. The scales agree with me, which is nice.

mortar.label: The mortar and pestle
mortar.moment: For cardamom and cinnamon. Ground fresh, a pinch goes a long way.

botanical-print.label: The chia plant
botanical-print.moment: That's chia in flower. It's a kind of sage, and the seeds come from those little purple spikes.

drawer-black-chia.label: Black chia
drawer-black-chia.moment: Black chia. Stir it into milk, wait five minutes, stir again, and leave it overnight.

drawer-white-chia.label: White chia
drawer-white-chia.moment: White chia. It looks prettier in a jar and tastes exactly the same as the black.

drawer-coconut-flakes.label: Coconut flakes
drawer-coconut-flakes.moment: Toast them in a dry pan for a couple of minutes, until they go golden. Don't walk away.

drawer-cacao-nibs.label: Cacao nibs
drawer-cacao-nibs.moment: Cacao nibs. Bitter and crunchy, like chocolate before anyone's added the sugar.

drawer-goji-berries.label: Goji berries
drawer-goji-berries.moment: Goji berries. Soak them for ten minutes and they plump right up.

drawer-matcha.label: Matcha
drawer-matcha.moment: Matcha. Half a teaspoon is plenty, and it'll wake you up.

chia-lane-window.label: The lane
chia-lane-window.moment: The same lane Sweet Spells looks out on. On a quiet day you can hear its music box across the hall.

atoms.title: The basic chia pudding
atoms.body: Three tablespoons of chia to a cup of any milk. Stir, wait five minutes, stir again so it doesn't clump, then into the fridge overnight. Everything else is toppings.

atoms.title: Matcha chia with lime and honey
atoms.body: Whisk half a teaspoon of matcha into a little warm milk first, then top up with cold milk and stir in the chia. A squeeze of lime and a drizzle of honey in the morning.

atoms.title: Chamomile and vanilla chia
atoms.body: Steep a chamomile teabag in half a cup of hot milk for five minutes, then add cold milk, vanilla and chia. A spoon of honey. Gentle enough for supper.

atoms.title: Chocolate chia with a dark chocolate layer
atoms.body: Stir a heaped spoon of cocoa and a little maple syrup into the milk before the chia goes in. Grate dark chocolate over the top and finish with cacao nibs.

atoms.title: Raspberry and mint chia, served cold
atoms.body: Mash a handful of raspberries with a few torn mint leaves and layer them with plain chia pudding in a jar. Eat it straight from the fridge.

atoms.title: Warm cinnamon and cardamom chia
atoms.body: Warm a cup of milk with cinnamon and a crushed cardamom pod, take out the pod, then stir in the chia and let it thicken for ten minutes off the heat. Like porridge, but quicker.

atoms.title: Mango and coconut chia
atoms.body: Make it with coconut milk, then blitz a ripe mango and spoon it over the top. Toasted coconut flakes and a squeeze of lime to finish.

atoms.title: Make tomorrow's breakfast tonight
atoms.body: Two minutes before bed: chia, milk, a stir, a lid. Tomorrow you open the fridge and breakfast is already made.

atoms.title: Why chia turns liquid into pudding
atoms.body: Each seed has a coat of soluble fibre that soaks up liquid and swells into a soft gel, many times the seed's own weight. That's the whole trick, and it's also why a jar of it is quite filling.
